references.cited_as: Workowski KA, Bachmann LH, Chan PA, et al. Sexually Transmitted Infections Treatment Guidelines, 2021. MMWR Recomm Rep. 2021;70(4):1-187.
references.version_or_date: CDC STI Treatment Guidelines 2021, MMWR Recomm Rep 70(4); BV page last reviewed July 22, 2021; read 2026-11-15
references.retrieved_with: PubMed get_article_metadata; PubMed get_full_text_article (PMC8344968; BV, vaginitis overview, trichomoniasis and VVC sections read); WebFetch of cdc.gov/std/treatment-guidelines/bv.htm to confirm the drug names that the PMC text drops from the regimen boxes; Scite verify_papers
references.notes: PMC text strips italicized drug and organism names, so regimen-box quotes lack drug names; the CDC page fetch (summarized, not verbatim) confirmed metronidazole, metronidazole 0.75% gel, clindamycin 2% cream (recommended) and clindamycin oral, clindamycin ovules, secnidazole, tinidazole (alternative) in that order. Empty citation parentheses removed from quotes. Scite flagged one contrasting citation about gonococcal loads, which does not bear on any BV claim here.

claims.text: Recommended regimens: metronidazole 500 mg orally twice daily for 7 days, metronidazole 0.75% gel one applicator (5 g) once daily for 5 days, clindamycin 2% cream one applicator at bedtime for 7 days (fixed 5 or 7 day courses)
claims.quote: 500 mg orally 2 times/day for 7 days or one full applicator (5 g) intravaginally, once daily for 5 days or one full applicator (5 g) intravaginally at bedtime for 7 days

claims.text: Alternative regimens: clindamycin 300 mg orally twice daily for 7 days; clindamycin ovules 100 mg at bedtime for 3 days
claims.quote: Alternative Regimens 300 mg orally 2 times/day for 7 days or 100 mg intravaginally once at bedtime for 3 days

claims.text: Alternative regimens: secnidazole 2 g oral granules single dose; tinidazole 2 g once daily for 2 days or 1 g once daily for 5 days
claims.quote: 2 g oral granules in a single dose or 2 g orally once daily for 2 days or 1 g orally once daily for 5 days

claims.text: CDC regimens are all antibiotics (metronidazole, clindamycin, tinidazole, secnidazole); secnidazole, tinidazole and other clindamycin forms are alternatives
claims.quote: Alternative regimens include secnidazole oral granules, multiple oral tinidazole regimens, or clindamycin (oral or intravaginal).

claims.text: Secnidazole granules sprinkled onto unsweetened applesauce, yogurt, or pudding
claims.quote: Oral granules should be sprinkled onto unsweetened applesauce, yogurt, or pudding before ingestion.

claims.text: Secnidazole phase 3: clinical cure days 21 to 30 was 53% vs 19% placebo; listed as alternative because of higher cost and lack of long-term outcomes (chart bars 53% and 19%)
claims.quote: BV clinical cure rates at days 21–30 were 53% in the secnidazole arm compared with 19% in the placebo arm (p<0.001). Secnidazole is listed as an alternative regimen, due to its higher cost and lack of long-term outcomes

claims.text: Chart: clindamycin 2% cream 7 days clinical cure 63.2% at days 21 to 30, in a trial CDC says had methodologic problems
claims.quote: Clindesse 2% vaginal cream single dose versus clindamycin 2% vaginal cream at bedtime for 7 days ... clinical cure at days 21–30 (64.3% versus 63.2%; p = 0.95); however, this study had methodologic problems.

claims.text: No studies directly compare oral and topical treatment
claims.quote: No data are available that directly compare the efficacy of oral and topical medications for treating BV.

claims.text: Clindamycin cream is oil based and can weaken latex condoms and diaphragms for 5 days after use
claims.quote: Clindamycin cream is oil based and might weaken latex condoms and diaphragms for 5 days after use

claims.text: Avoid sex or use condoms consistently and correctly during treatment; douching might increase relapse and has no data supporting it for treatment or symptom relief
claims.quote: Women should be advised to refrain from sexual activity or to use condoms consistently and correctly during the BV treatment regimen. Douching might increase the risk for relapse, and no data support use of douching for treatment or symptom relief.

claims.text: No studies support probiotic or Lactobacillus products as an add-on or replacement for BV treatment
claims.quote: Studies have evaluated the clinical and microbiologic efficacy of intravaginal and other probiotic formulations to treat BV and restore normal vaginal microbiota; overall, no studies support these products as an adjunctive or replacement therapy for women with BV.

claims.text: Lactin-V lowered recurrence in a trial but is not yet FDA cleared or commercially available
claims.quote: reported a substantially lower incidence of BV recurrence at 12 weeks in the Lactin-V arm, compared with placebo; however this medication is not yet FDA cleared or commercially available.

claims.text: After a first recurrence, retreatment with the same recommended regimen is acceptable, or a different recommended regimen can be considered
claims.quote: Using a different recommended treatment regimen can be considered for women who have a recurrence; however, retreatment with the same recommended regimen is an acceptable approach for treating persistent or recurrent BV after the first occurrence

claims.text: For multiple recurrences, metronidazole gel twice weekly for more than 3 months reduces recurrence, but the benefit does not persist after stopping
claims.quote: For women with multiple recurrences after completion of a recommended regimen, either 0.75% metronidazole gel or 750 mg metronidazole vaginal suppository twice weekly for >3 months has been reported to reduce recurrences, although this benefit does not persist

claims.text: Limited-data option for multiple recurrences: 7-day oral nitroimidazole, then boric acid 600 mg vaginally daily for 21 days, then twice-weekly 0.75% gel for 4 to 6 months
claims.quote: an oral nitroimidazole (metronidazole or tinidazole 500 mg 2 times/day for 7 days), followed by intravaginal boric acid 600 mg daily for 21 days and suppressive 0.75% metronidazole gel twice weekly for 4–6 months, might be an option

claims.text: Follow-up not needed if symptoms resolve; return if symptoms recur because persistent or recurrent BV is common
claims.quote: Follow-up visits are unnecessary if symptoms resolve. Because persistent or recurrent BV is common, women should be advised to return for evaluation if symptoms recur.

claims.text: CDC 2021 does not recommend routine partner treatment
claims.quote: Data from earlier clinical trials indicate that a woman’s response to therapy and the likelihood of relapse or recurrence are not affected by treatment of her sex partner. Therefore, routine treatment of sex partners is not recommended.

claims.text: An earlier trial of 7-day oral metronidazole for male partners did not reduce recurrence
claims.quote: A phase 3 multicenter randomized double-blinded trial evaluating the efficacy of a 7-day oral metronidazole regimen versus placebo for treatment of male sex partners of women with recurrent BV did not find that male partner treatment reduced BV recurrence

claims.text: BV: normal lactic-acid-producing species replaced by high concentrations of anaerobic bacteria; a notable feature is a polymicrobial biofilm on vaginal epithelial cells
claims.quote: replacement of normal hydrogen peroxide and lactic-acid–producing species in the vagina with high concentrations of anaerobic bacteria ... A notable feature is the appearance of a polymicrobial biofilm on vaginal epithelial cells

claims.text: Medical history alone is not enough for accurate diagnosis and can lead to the wrong medication
claims.quote: Obtaining a medical history alone has been reported to be insufficient for accurate diagnosis of vaginitis and can lead to inappropriate administration of medication

claims.text: Unnecessary or unapproved use of over-the-counter vaginal products is common and can delay treatment of the actual cause
claims.quote: Unnecessary or unapproved use of over-the-counter preparations is common and can lead to a delay in treatment of other vulvovaginitis etiologies, which can result in adverse outcomes.

claims.text: In the office, pH, a KOH test and microscopy can often identify the cause
claims.quote: In the clinician’s office, the cause of vaginal symptoms can often be determined by pH, a potassium hydroxide (KOH) test, and microscopic examination of a wet mount of fresh samples of vaginal discharge.

claims.text: BV NAATs can be run on clinician-collected or self-collected vaginal swabs, in women with symptoms
claims.quote: They can be performed on either clinician- or self-collected vaginal specimens ... BV NAATs should be used among symptomatic women only

claims.text: Trichomoniasis can also raise vaginal pH and cause similar discharge and odor; revisit the diagnosis if a plan fails
claims.quote: an elevated pH (i.e., >4.5) is common with BV or trichomoniasis ... samples that emit an amine odor immediately upon application of KOH suggest BV or trichomoniasis

claims.text: Some women have short-lived changes in vaginal bacteria while others have them for longer; CDC recommends treatment for women with symptoms
claims.quote: Certain women experience transient vaginal microbial changes, whereas others experience them for longer intervals ... Treatment for BV is recommended for women with symptoms.

claims.text: BV is linked to higher risk of acquiring STIs and to pregnancy complications
claims.quote: Women with BV are at increased risk for STI acquisition, such as HIV, HPV, and HSV-2; complications after gynecologic surgery; complications of pregnancy; and recurrence of BV

claims.text: BV is associated with multiple or new partners, lack of condom use and douching
claims.quote: BV is associated with having multiple male sex partners, female partners, sexual relationships with more than one person, a new sex partner, lack of condom use, douching

claims.text: Hormonal contraception does not increase BV risk and might protect against it
claims.quote: Hormonal contraception does not increase risk for BV and might protect against BV development

claims.text: Treat all symptomatic pregnant women; symptomatic BV linked to premature rupture of membranes, preterm birth, intra-amniotic infection, postpartum endometritis
claims.quote: BV treatment is recommended for all symptomatic pregnant women because symptomatic BV has been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including premature rupture of membranes, preterm birth, intra-amniotic infection, and postpartum endometritis

claims.text: Metronidazole poses low risk in pregnancy; vaginal clindamycin is safe; tinidazole should be avoided
claims.quote: newer data demonstrate that this treatment approach is safe for pregnant women ... These data indicate that metronidazole therapy poses low risk during pregnancy ... Thus, tinidazole should be avoided during pregnancy

claims.text: Secnidazole should be avoided in pregnancy
claims.quote: Data are insufficient regarding efficacy and adverse effects of secnidazole, Clindesse 2% vaginal cream, metronidazole 1.3% vaginal gel, and 750-mg vaginal metronidazole tablets during pregnancy; thus, their use should be avoided.

claims.text: Routine BV screening of asymptomatic pregnant women is not recommended for preventing preterm birth
claims.quote: Therefore, routine screening for BV among asymptomatic pregnant women at high or low risk for preterm delivery for preventing preterm birth is not recommended.

claims.text: Symptoms that could be BV in pregnancy are a reason to contact the obstetric clinician rather than wait (inferred from the recommendation to treat all symptomatic pregnant women)
claims.quote: BV treatment is recommended for all symptomatic pregnant women

claims.text: Tea tree oil and yogurt inserts are not part of any CDC regimen (read from the recommended and alternative regimen lists, which contain only antibiotics)
claims.quote: Alternative regimens include secnidazole oral granules, multiple oral tinidazole regimens, or clindamycin (oral or intravaginal).

references.cited_as: Bradshaw CS, Morton AN, Hocking J, et al. J Infect Dis. 2006;193(11):1478-1486.
references.record_title: High recurrence rates of bacterial vaginosis over the course of 12 months after oral metronidazole therapy and factors associated with recurrence.

Scite flagged one contrasting citation (10.1186/s12879-015-0971-3) reporting better 6-month cure in other trials; the page states 58 percent as one cohort, not a universal rate.

claims.text: In one Australian cohort treated with oral metronidazole, 58 percent had BV again within 12 months
claims.quote: BV was treated with 400 mg of oral metronidazole twice a day for 7 days ... Sixty-eight women (58% [95% confidence interval {CI}, 49%-66%]) had a recurrence of BV (NS 7-10)

claims.text: Recurrence is common and current treatment does not prevent it in most women
claims.quote: Current recommended treatment is not preventing the recurrence of BV or abnormal vaginal flora in the majority of women

references.cited_as: Sobel JD, Ferris D, Schwebke J, et al. Am J Obstet Gynecol. 2006;194(5):1283-1289.
references.record_title: Suppressive antibacterial therapy with 0.75% metronidazole vaginal gel to prevent recurrent bacterial vaginosis.

claims.text: Women with recurrent BV who responded to 10 days of gel used twice-weekly gel for 16 weeks; recurrence 25.5% vs 59.1% placebo during suppression
claims.quote: initial 10-day open-label metronidazole gel in which asymptomatic responders randomly assigned to receive twice weekly metronidazole vaginal gel or placebo for 16 weeks ... recurrent bacterial vaginosis occurred in 13 women (25.5%) receiving metronidazole and 26 (59.1%) receiving placebo

claims.text: Across 28 weeks recurrence was 51% vs 75%; vaginal yeast infections more common with gel
claims.quote: During the entire 28-week follow-up, recurrence occurred in 26 (51.0%) on treatment compared with 33 (75%) on placebo ... secondary vaginal candidiasis occurred significantly more often in metronidazole-treated women

claims.text: Suppressive gel lowers recurrence while used; randomized trial support
claims.quote: Suppressive therapy with twice-weekly metronidazole gel achieves a significant reduction in the recurrence rate of bacterial vaginosis; however, secondary vaginal candidiasis is common.

references.cited_as: Reichman O, Akins R, Sobel JD. Sex Transm Dis. 2009;36(11):732-734.
references.record_title: Boric acid addition to suppressive antimicrobial therapy for recurrent bacterial vaginosis.

claims.text: Boric acid is part of a limited-data regimen for multiple recurrences: 7-day oral nitroimidazole, 21 days of boric acid 600 mg, then twice-weekly gel; uncontrolled data
claims.quote: Uncontrolled, nonrandomized, retrospective chart review of patients with RBV treated with 7 days of oral nitroimidazole; followed by 21 days of intravaginal BA 600 mg/day and if in remission treated with metronidazole gel twice weekly for 16 weeks.

references.cited_as: Cohen CR, Wierzbicki MR, French AL, et al. N Engl J Med. 2020;382(20):1906-1915.

claims.text: Lactin-V (L. crispatus CTV-05) after metronidazole gel: recurrence by week 12 was 30% vs 45% placebo
claims.quote: recurrence of bacterial vaginosis by week 12 occurred in 46 participants (30%) in the Lactin-V group and in 34 participants (45%) in the placebo group

claims.text: Lactin-V was used vaginally after a course of metronidazole gel
claims.quote: who had completed a course of vaginal metronidazole gel as part of the eligibility requirements were randomly assigned, in a 2:1 ratio, to receive vaginally administered Lactin-V or placebo for 11 weeks

references.cited_as: Vodstrcil LA, Plummer EL, Fairley CK, et al. N Engl J Med. 2025;392(10):947-957.

claims.quote: recurrence occurred in 24 of 69 women (35%) in the partner-treatment group ... and in 43 of 68 women (63%) in the control group

claims.quote: the woman received first-line recommended antimicrobial agents and the male partner received oral and topical antimicrobial treatment (metronidazole 400-mg tablets and 2% clindamycin cream applied to penile skin, both twice daily for 7 days)

claims.text: Trial stopped early because treating the woman alone was inferior

claims.text: Trial enrolled women with BV in a monogamous relationship with a male partner

claims.text: Treated men reported nausea, headache and metallic taste

claims.quote: achieved a satisfactory response (BV cure ≤2 Amsel criteria) in 92 of 93 available patients. Thereafter, a maintenance metronidazole gel prevented symptomatic BV recurrence in 69.6% of compliant patients at 6-month follow-up.

claims.text: Uncontrolled retrospective review with frequent loss to follow-up
claims.quote: Results reflect standard of clinic care in this uncontrolled retrospective cohort analysis ... Frequent loss to follow-up in this long-term study influenced efficacy evaluation.

claims.quote: As part of the US registration package, two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical studies were conducted ... Single-dose secnidazole 2 g was statistically superior to placebo on all primary and secondary efficacy outcomes in both trials

claims.quote: there is an absolute concordance in the carriage of biofilm-associated (cohesive) G. vaginalis between women with bacterial vaginosis and their partners
